audit_metadata.methodology: Direct source inspection (file:line citation required for every claim), safe local command execution (cargo check/audit, forge test, git log, grep sweeps), cross-verification of the repository's own extensive self-audit trail (GAP_REPORT.md, TESTNET_GAP_LEDGER.md, MASTER_CHECKLIST_STATUS.md, FEATURE_REGISTRY.toml) rather than trusting it at face value, per the repository's own AGENTS.md instruction to treat prior reports as unverified until reproduced.
audit_metadata.scope_note: This is a time-boxed, single-session independent audit. Several sub-areas explicitly requested in the audit brief (per-attack-category attack-tree diagrams, blank benchmark templates for every unmeasured metric, multi-host consensus re-execution, full smart-contract-by-smart-contract line coverage) were not exhausted; those are marked BLOCKED / not verified this session rather than fabricated. No node was booted, no funds moved, no destructive commands run, no secrets printed.

verification_commands_run.result: FAILS - compile_error! on mutually-exclusive feature combination (test-verifier + production in x3-finality-oracle) - this is a correct guard, not a bug, but means --all-features cannot be used to verify 'compiles clean'

findings.title: Node's built-in wallet RPC service is 100% fabricated and unconditionally live
findings.summary: wallet_createWallet, wallet_importWallet, wallet_signTransaction, wallet_getBalance, wallet_backupWallet return fabricated data: hardcoded balances, a fake 'signature' that is literally a substring of the input, and the public Hardhat/Ganache default test mnemonic when none is supplied. Registered unconditionally on every full node's RPC surface with no dev-only gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Any client calling wallet_createWallet without its own mnemonic gets a well-known, already-compromised seed phrase and a non-cryptographic pseudo-address (first 40 chars of the mnemonic string). Any client trusting wallet_signTransaction's output as a real signature will have it silently rejected on-chain, or worse, build automation that trusts the fabricated 'success' response and displayed fake balances ($3750.00 X3, $8304.50 ETH, hardcoded).
findings.operational_impact: Reputational/fund-safety risk if ever exposed externally or integrated by a client; violates the audit's explicit prohibition on hard-coded success responses and fabricated metrics in production paths.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove wallet_* custodial methods from the node RPC surface entirely, or gate behind an explicit --enable-demo-wallet-rpc flag that refuses non-dev chain specs.
findings.verification_after_fix: Assert wallet_* methods return Method not found on --chain testnet/mainnet specs.

findings.title: Feature registry's top-scored entry cites tests that do not exist; the consistency checker cannot detect this
findings.summary: required_tests for atomic_kernel (readiness_score 85, highest in the registry) lists halt_blocks_new_mint, halt_blocks_new_transfer, halt_blocks_new_swap, halt_allows_refund, halt_allows_recovery. None exist anywhere in the repository under any name. scripts/check-readiness-consistency.sh only validates score-contradictions and crate_or_service path existence - it never checks required_tests for real existence.
findings.failure_scenario: Any registry entry's readiness score can be inflated indefinitely by citing fictional test names, and the automated gate designed to keep the registry honest will still report PASS.
findings.operational_impact: Undermines the evidentiary basis for every readiness score in FEATURE_REGISTRY.toml, not just this one entry.
findings.evidence_quality: Confirmed by static inspection (repo-wide grep, zero matches)
findings.recommended_fix: Add a check to check-readiness-consistency.sh that greps for each required_tests entry as a real #[test] fn <name> in the cited crate_or_service path, hard-failing if absent. Reclassify atomic_kernel to PARTIAL pending real tests or a corrected citation.
findings.verification_after_fix: check-readiness-consistency.sh fails when a required_tests entry is fictional.

findings.title: Unauthenticated public validator-slashing extrinsic
findings.summary: report_misbehavior(origin, validator, reason) requires only ensure_signed (any signed account) and directly slashes the named validator - no cryptographic evidence, no proof type, no rate limit, no dispute window. Contrast with the properly proof-gated GRANDPA equivocation path in runtime/src/lib.rs:205-224.
findings.failure_scenario: Any signed, even low-value, account can costlessly grief/censor any validator by repeatedly calling report_misbehavior, degrading consensus liveness by shrinking the active validator set.
findings.operational_impact: Denial-of-service / censorship vector against validator liveness on any network where this pallet is live (wired into every construct_runtime! variant).
findings.recommended_fix: Require report_misbehavior to carry real on-chain-verifiable evidence per SlashReason, or restrict origin to a privileged reporter/committee with a challenge window.
findings.verification_after_fix: Test asserting a bare report_misbehavior call with no evidence is rejected.

findings.title: Real validator authoring seeds and a plaintext testnet private key remain permanently recoverable from git history
findings.summary: Commit fbd4613b removed these files from the working tree but its own commit message states history has NOT been rewritten and the real rotation (filter-branch/BFG + offline key regeneration) has not happened yet.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who has cloned, or clones before a history rewrite, has the AURA/GRANDPA seeds and a Sepolia private key.
findings.operational_impact: Any value ever sent to addresses derived from these keys, or any validator identity built on them, is compromised.
findings.recommended_fix: Perform the history rewrite (filter-branch/BFG) and rotate all affected keys offline via subkey before any public tag.
findings.verification_after_fix: git log --all -- <path> returns zero hits after rewrite; new keys generated offline.

findings.title: Single env-var-controlled key has effectively unilateral wrapped-asset mint authority
findings.summary: The X3_SUBMITTER_SEED signer both submits the kernel cross-VM operation and proposes-and-immediately-executes (pallet_collective threshold: 1) register_wrapped_asset and mint_wrapped. No second signer, no quorum, no timelock.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever controls X3_SUBMITTER_SEED can mint wrapped assets unilaterally on any network where the bridge relay path is reachable.
findings.operational_impact: Currently mitigated only by ExternalBridgesEnabled=false at genesis (verified enforced elsewhere in this audit) - this is a governance gate, not a code-level quorum.
findings.recommended_fix: Require a real multi-signer quorum (threshold > 1) for wrapped-asset register/mint before enabling external bridges.
findings.verification_after_fix: Council call with threshold=1 rejected; require >=2 independent signers.

findings.title: Validator set is fully centralized (root-controlled); understated in top-level docs
findings.summary: set_validators is ensure_root-only. No pallet_staking, bonding, or nomination exists anywhere in the runtime. LAUNCH_SCOPE.md's gated-out list omits this by silence rather than stating it explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: N/A (not an exploit) - a decentralization/trust-model transparency gap.
findings.operational_impact: Any claim of validator decentralization is currently false; single root key controls the validator set.
findings.recommended_fix: State explicitly in LAUNCH_SCOPE.md that permissionless staking/bonding is NOT IMPLEMENTED, deferred to M3, the same way other gated features are called out.

findings.title: quantum-crypto's Kyber/Dilithium modules are not real post-quantum cryptography
findings.summary: No pqcrypto/liboqs dependency exists. Key generation is Sha3_512("KYBER_KEYGEN" + seed) - the code's own comment says 'Simplified key generation'. No lattice arithmetic anywhere. Byte sizes mimic real Kyber, giving a false impression of standards conformance.
findings.failure_scenario: If ever used believing it provides post-quantum security, it provides none.
findings.operational_impact: Correctly gated out of RC-1 via pq-experimental feature flag (verified) - mitigating factor - but the code's naming is actively misleading regardless of gating.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename to clearly indicate mock/placeholder status, or delete until real PQC bindings (pqcrypto-kyber etc.) are integrated.
findings.verification_after_fix: Documentation/naming review; real dependency added if kept.
blocks: mainnet (only if ever un-gated without a real implementation)

findings.title: Solana HTLC program (x3_htlc) has zero tests
findings.summary: Unlike every sibling SVM program (5 of 6 have inline #[test] coverage, 74 tests total), x3_htlc has none. HTLC atomicity is listed as a 'Critical X3 System' in the repo's own AGENTS.md.
findings.failure_scenario: An untested HTLC implementation is the highest-risk category of smart contract for fund loss (hash/timelock logic errors directly cause stuck or stolen funds).
findings.operational_impact: Blocks confident use of the SVM atomic-swap path.
findings.recommended_fix: Write unit + integration tests for x3_htlc before treating the SVM atomic-swap path as audit-ready.
findings.verification_after_fix: cargo test / anchor test passes with real HTLC-specific coverage.

findings.title: Gateway /health endpoint is an unconditional 200 OK; registry's per-feature health endpoints don't exist
findings.summary: async fn health() returns StatusCode::OK unconditionally, ignoring a real db.healthy() check that exists in the same crate but is never called from this handler. FEATURE_REGISTRY.toml claims /health/atomic-kernel, /health/atomic-router, /health/runtime, /health/atomic-gateway - none of these paths exist anywhere in the codebase.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator or load balancer trusting /health as a real readiness signal will route traffic to a node whose DB or chain-sync is actually broken.
findings.operational_impact: Classic fake health check pattern; misleads operational tooling.
findings.recommended_fix: Wire db.healthy() and a chain-head-staleness check into /health; build or remove the claimed per-feature endpoints.
findings.verification_after_fix: Integration test that stops the DB and confirms /health returns non-200.

findings.title: No dynamic fee-market response to congestion
findings.summary: FeeMultiplierUpdate = () means fees never rise under sustained mempool pressure.
findings.failure_scenario: Reduced spam resistance relative to stock Substrate chains using TargetedFeeAdjustment (bounded pool + ban-time still apply as a backstop).
findings.operational_impact: Minor liveness/spam risk under sustained load.
findings.verification_after_fix: Load test showing fee increase under sustained mempool pressure.

findings.title: X3ExternalGateway.sol lacks ReentrancyGuard
findings.summary: No nonReentrant modifier, unlike Treasury.sol in the same repo. Mitigated by SafeERC20 + onlySupportedToken allowlist, but a non-standard allowlisted token with transfer-hook semantics could still reenter.
findings.failure_scenario: Reentrancy via a maliciously-designed but allowlisted token.
findings.operational_impact: Low today given allowlisting; would become material if token listing is ever decentralized.
findings.verification_after_fix: Reentrancy test against a malicious mock token.

findings.title: External bridge root registration accepts any non-empty byte string as 'proof'
findings.summary: register_bridge_root's proof validation is ensure!(!proof.is_empty()). Currently low-risk because the whole surface is behind ExternalBridgesEnabled=false (verified enforced) and root-only origin.
findings.failure_scenario: If bridges are ever enabled without fixing this, a privileged account could register an arbitrary/incorrect root.
findings.operational_impact: Must be fixed before governance ever flips ExternalBridgesEnabled to true.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace with real independent SPV/consensus verification of the submitted root before enabling.
findings.verification_after_fix: Test that a forged/incorrect root is rejected.
blocks: mainnet (specifically, before external bridges can be safely enabled)

findings.title: Storage migrations are unproven scaffolding, not demonstrated migration capability
findings.component: 10 pallets' migrations.rs (agent-accounts, agent-memory, atomic-trade-engine, evolution-core, governance, meme-overlord, svm-runtime, treasury, x3-kernel, x3-verifier)
findings.summary: Every migrations.rs examined is an identical boilerplate StorageVersion bump with no field-transform logic; none has ever been exercised against a real schema change.
findings.failure_scenario: The first real breaking schema change to any of these pallets is untested territory.
findings.operational_impact: Runtime upgrade risk understated by 'migrations exist' framing.
findings.recommended_fix: Exercise at least one real storage-layout change through try-runtime rehearsal before relying on this pattern for mainnet.
findings.verification_after_fix: try-runtime on-runtime-upgrade passes against a deliberately changed schema.

findings.title: Supply-ledger O(n) per-block iteration is a latent liveness risk at scale
findings.summary: on_finalize iterates every tracked asset every block with no pagination/amortization.
findings.failure_scenario: Could stall block production once thousands of assets are listed (token-factory/launchpad growth).
findings.operational_impact: Not exploitable today at RC-1 bounded asset count.
findings.recommended_fix: Add amortized/paginated checking or a per-block cap before permissionless asset listing scales.
findings.verification_after_fix: Benchmark on_finalize weight vs. asset count.

findings.title: srtool reproducible build pinned by tag, not digest
findings.summary: SRTOOL_IMAGE defaults to paritytech/srtool:1.75.0 (a mutable tag) rather than a sha256 digest.
findings.failure_scenario: A tag can theoretically be repointed upstream, weakening build reproducibility guarantees.
findings.verification_after_fix: Build reproduced bit-for-bit from the pinned digest on two machines.

findings.title: Mempool flood resilience unverified
findings.summary: Bounded pool config is real but no sustained-flood/adversarial-mempool test was found or executed.
findings.failure_scenario: Unknown behavior under sustained adversarial load.
findings.recommended_fix: Run a dedicated load test before public-testnet claims.

findings.title: Orphaned patches/sp-state-machine directory is dead weight
findings.summary: Not referenced by any [patch] entry in Cargo.toml; misleads a reader into thinking state-machine internals were deliberately modified.
findings.operational_impact: Documentation-hazard clutter, matches MASTER_CHECKLIST_STATUS.md's own admission of 'orphaned folders' clutter.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete or document why it's kept.

findings.title: TREASURY_POLICY.md / MASTER_CHECKLIST_STATUS.md misdescribe Treasury.sol's access control
findings.summary: Docs claim 'routeFee is callable by anyone'; the tracked contract has always had onlyOwner on that function per git history. The real, still-valid risk is different: no on-chain guarantee the owner is a multisig.
findings.failure_scenario: An external reviewer trusting the doc's literal wording flags a non-issue and could miss the real issue.
findings.operational_impact: Documentation-accuracy issue, not a code vulnerability.
findings.evidence_quality: Confirmed by static inspection + git log
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the doc's wording; keep pursuing its own correct recommendation (Safe multisig owner).

findings.title: VRF has no real production randomness provider, but correctly fails closed
findings.summary: Only MockVrfProvider (dev/test-gated) and VrfNotConfigured (production default, always errors) exist. No real VRF construction implemented yet. This is a commendable fail-closed pattern, not a silent insecure fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: fulfill_randomness will always fail with VrfGenerationFailed on a real production binary today - a functional gap, not a security hole.
findings.operational_impact: Any feature depending on x3-vrf for production randomness cannot function yet.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement a real VRF construction (e.g. schnorrkel's VRF, already a transitive dependency) as the production provider.
findings.verification_after_fix: fulfill_randomness succeeds on a non-dev production build with real proof verification.
blocks: any feature depending on real randomness
